So people were giving all their things for as long as they had anything, and then at one point he said if I find anyone with any money left, I'm going to build -- bring dogs now and they are going to find out whether you have some money left. So people again gave more money. Then he left and then there weren't anything left there. That happened in the morning. I skipped that. I didn't tell you about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And during the time that you were there from the 12th into the 13th, the afternoon of the 13th, were you provided with any food or water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Water, yes. From the morning. I told you. We had enough water in water bottles, plastic ones, up to five litres. There was enough water. As for food, we didn't ask for any, they didn't give us any, but nobody really felt like eating because we were having such a hard time that no one could eat. We could only drink water. When we saw what was being done to us, no one really felt like eating any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the time that you boarded the buses, was it dark outside? Was it light outside? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I remember. Before it was dark, we boarded the buses, but this was just before dark so we waited for the lights to be turned on, we were waiting there, in all the buses, we didn't go anywhere. When the lights were on, then the buses set out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How many buses were there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Six buses, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And about what time, if you can estimate, did you set out from Bratunac, from this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Well, between 8.00 and 9.00. That's when it got dark too. I cannot tell you the exact hour, but in any rate when the first lights were turned on in town, that's when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you -- did you stop anywhere en route to the -- your ultimate destination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: We stopped at Drinjaca, perhaps we were there for a few hours on the buses, and we asked the driver why are we standing here? What are we waiting for here? And he said, I can just see the bus in front of me. When it sets out, I will follow it. If you know, then I know where we are going too. I don't know a thing, he said. So we just sat there on the bus and then when the bus before us started, then we started too.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Where were you taken, if you can recall the route that you took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: We got out to the road that leads to Serbia from Bratunac. We got to the Drina. On the Drina there is a bridge crossing over to Serbia. We did not cross that bridge. We turned left. We went down the Drina to Zvornik. We were in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you stop in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: No, no. We didn't stop in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: We passed through Zvornik. It's called Karakaj, this place, so when we were near Karakaj we went left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how long did you continue in that direction, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: That I cannot tell, how long it was that we were driving. We stopped by a school at any rate and we saw a group of Serb soldiers there, perhaps ten or 15 of them in this group that was standing there, the buses stopped, the bus in front of us stopped so we stopped too. Then the driver said, "You'll be getting out here for sure." In front of us we already saw men getting off and they were entering a gym of a school that was by the road. As they got out, the buses in front of us, the people from the buses in front of us, then we got out too. One by one. And there were six buses or whatever. And then we all got out and entered that gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: About what time did you arrive at this school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: It's possible that it was 2.00, after midnight. I'm not sure about that, though. At any rate, it was after midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that would have been on the night of the 13th of July into the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Could you describe the inside of this gymnasium, as you've described it? Just briefly, if you could.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: On the left-hand side there was a house, a residential house. Before that house, we got out of the bus. We walked in front of that house, the gym was in front, and on the right-hand side there was this school. The school door was -- now, was the gym linked to the school or not? I don't know. I couldn't figure that out. But at any rate, it had its own entrance into -- well, the gym had its own entrance. As we went by, and to the left, we entered the gym straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, if you don't mind, could we have the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This would be fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 25 minutes break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were supposed to take one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I've exceeded my time. I thought I had estimated an hour and a half, but apparently that's not what's reflected in front of you. So I apologise for that. I shouldn't be longer than 15 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just before I continue where we left off, I wanted to ask you, witness, you indicated on page 46, in the transcript, that you were told that the warehouse you were in in Bratunac was behind the Vuk Karadzic school. Can you tell us when it is that you heard that for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I saw that, that we passed by a school, and that then we got to the warehouse. And that's how I saw that it was passed a school. Somebody told me that this was a cooperative warehouse, that some agricultural cooperative had used that warehouse. And then when they made new warehouses in Kravica, they abandoned this one and moved the cooperative to the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when did you learn the name of the school that it was behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I knew the school from before, but I was told in Bratunac, I knew about the school before, but I never went there but I was told that the name of the school was Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That same night, on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to go back to where we were. I think I left off, and I'd asked to you describe the inside of the gym you were taken to on the night of the 13th into the 14th of July. So tell us what you were able to observe when you went inside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I saw in front, as I was entering the gym, that there was the hoop to play basketball. On the right side there were the windows, halfway up the walls of the gym, and then some equipment that was around the windows. On the left side, the windows were also placed quite high on the walls of the gym, not at around the middle. And then a little bit before, to the left side, there was the side door to the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I please have in e-court 65 ter 1697. I just want to show a photograph, if I could. Do you see this photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recognise what's depicted in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us what you see? Tell us what you recognise about this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I recognise the hoop, the entrance door, the side door where this person is bent over, next to the side door, this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And the entrance door you're referring to is, is that the other door in the photograph? Or other opening, I should say. There are two openings. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: This door, where this person is bent over, that's the side door. That's where we would exit the gym. And the other door was where we would enter the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that, Witness. Could I show you 65 ter 1693, please? That's another photograph. Do you see the photograph in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I think this is the side door and this is the basketball hoop.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. And could I just have in e-court, please, 65 ter 1691? Do you see this photograph now in front of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: We see the school and the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And which is the school and which is the gym, if you could just indicate which side of the photograph you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: The school is on the right-hand side and the gym is on the left-hand side. Between the school and the gym, you can enter the gym through the door, entrance door.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. If I could, I'd like to show you 65 ter 1698. Do you see the photograph in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: This is not quite clear to me, but I think that this is where the TAM small truck was parked, and this is where we exited and entered the TAM, using this door.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. I just want to continue with your testimony at this point. During the time that you were inside the gym, can you describe the kind of conditions that you were held in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: While there were just a few of us, the ones who arrived with the four buses, the conditions were all right. But when the warehouse got full and when the last trucks and buses had brought people in, and when no more could enter the gym, then we were told to stand up, to face the door, and to step backwards, and then we were stepping backwards, and they were firing over our heads and saying, "Back, back, back, we will shoot you." And that's what we kept doing until we made room for even the last ones to enter, and then when they entered we were told to sit down. And then when we sat down, those who managed to sit down first were able to sit down. The others could only sit in our lap. There was no more floor space for others to sit and that's when it got very stuffy, tight, and we wanted to suffocate.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was it that the last people arrived, the last prisoners arrived, at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I'm not sure. It's been a long time. How can I remember everything? But it was about 10.00 when they arrived, the last ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: 10.00 in the morning or at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: In the morning, in the morning, at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you given any food or water to drink while you were held in this gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Nothing, nothing. They gave us nothing then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you see any interactions between the soldiers and the prisoners while you were held inside the gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: No, no, no. The prisoners just said, "Why are you making us suffocate here? Why aren't you taking us for an exchange?" The soldiers said that they knew nothing about an exchange. They said that they cannot say anything as to what's going to happen to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did anyone complain about the conditions to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: One man jumped up, just this one man, who complained and said that he didn't want to stay there any longer, that he suffocating, why are they torturing him? And they said, you come out here, and cool off a bit. He went out through the entrance door where we had all entered, a burst of gunfire was heard, and he never returned again. That was the only rebellion there was. That was the only person who got out. Then nobody complained. We all kept quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, at some point, were you directed to leave this gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes. When General Mladic came, then he said this to us. We were told or rather the guards told us, they said now you're going to have Mladic come here and you ask him what's going to happen to you, and he appeared again with a few soldiers at the door and we said why are you making us suffocate here? Why are you torturing us? Why don't you take us somewhere? And he said to us, what can I do about it when your government doesn't want you and I have to take care of you? He said, now, some of you will go to Fikret Abdic and others will go to Bijeljina. And we said, we have no water, and he said when you go out then you'll have water to drink, you won't have any water before that. He said that and he went out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And at some point after that, were you provided with water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Whoever went out realised that there was water there and they would be blindfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you see how these people were provided with the water or how it is that the blindfolds --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: They had some kind of buckets or something. There was this table out there. When it was my turn, the soldiers would take buckets, bring water, and then take them away again when they were empty. Then there was this little thing, it wasn't plastic but it was a metal pot, a little pot or a little glass like thing, and that is how we'd get some water.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And how were these -- how were the prisoners blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Before that when we were supposed to go out, two soldiers brought this kind of thing. Some kind of cloth cut into pieces. And they put it by the entrance door, and they said to these two men now who is going to be the two men tying people's eyes? And then you'll have water to drink. And then two of our men volunteered. They got up and that is how our people got up, one by one. Now, did they first drink water? Were they blindfolded? Doesn't matter. They would get blindfolded, they would drink water, and then we would leave the hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember anything distinctive about these particular soldiers that brought the blindfolds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I don't remember anything. They were in camouflage uniforms like the other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you blindfolded yourself at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes. When I was getting out. That's when they blindfolded me. I had some water to drink, and then I went towards the little TAM truck. The floor was so high up that it was on the same level as the door of the TAM truck, so we didn't have to climb up on to the little truck. You would just walk in. When I got on to the little TAM truck, I sat there right next to the back. It was covered with a tarpaulin, but the tarpaulin was taken back so we could see everything that was going on from behind. When the little TAM truck set out, the red car that was behind us followed us. One soldier had an olive green grey uniform. He did not have an a camouflage uniform. He sat next to the driver. There was this red car, and he opened the door and he held the door with his right-hand, and in his left hand there was an automatic rifle. And he held that between the door and the car, and he said don't talk, don't remove your blindfolds. And that is the way it was as we were travelling along the road. Then we turned off into a pasture, and we saw lots of dead bodies. We thought that we would stop there too but we didn't. We went further on. When the little TAM truck stopped again and turned off, then we saw another heap of dead bodies. That's when the truck stopped. Two soldiers opened the back. I was the last one sitting there and then I would be the first to get off, and then he took my foot and told me where to stand and where to get out, and not to talk. That's how they got us all off the truck. As soon as the truck left, bursts of gunfire were opened and they shot in our backs. So the man behind me fell on me. I fell on my stomach and that is how I remained, lying there. They were shooting, people were moaning and showing some signs of life, once they all fell, this was individual. When the gunfire stopped, they moved away, I didn't dare look because they could see then that I hadn't been killed. So I just kept quiet until the other truck came and brought in these other people. Then say about five or six metres away from me, the little TAM truck turned to the road where we were. Then I turned my head a bit, and I saw them getting them off the TAM truck and lining them up in four lines. As soon as this truck left, they immediately started shooting at them, bursts of gunfire. That's how they killed them too and that's how this went on in succession. As soon as the red car would come, then it would go back, they would wait for the little TAM truck. The little TAM truck would stay there until it was unloaded. Then this went on for a while until once the red car came, parked, the little TAM truck turned off, and General Mladic was there and the soldier from the red car with the automatic rifle following the buses, he stood by the car until they were all unloaded from the truck, until they were all killed. The TAM truck left, and then when everybody was dead, Mladic sat in the back seat of the car and the soldier with the rifle sat in the front seat next to the driver, and then they went away. That's how the killing continued. Behind me there was a yellow excavator that was digging a grave. When it got dark, it was a bit cloudy and there was a bit of a drizzle. Another excavator came and that excavator moved away a bit, they stood next to each other, they turned on their headlights, and then the two TAM trucks were coming in and they were killing people under these lights. One little TAM truck would go away and the other one would come in. The red car would escort the TAM truck until the other one would be unloaded, so it was the same car escorting both trucks. That's what went on until sometime at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just ask you about how many people can you estimate were in that gym with you before this killing started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: When the gym was full, when the last group arrived, as we were sitting all next to each other, we asked what do you think, how many people are there in this gym? When you would look around you would just see heads and it's a big gym. No one said that there were less than 2 and a half thousand people there. We didn't really count, though. I cannot say that. That's the way it seemed to us. It seemed to us that no one had stayed behind, that everybody came to that gym. There were that many of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you've obviously survived this. When you made -- how was it that you managed to make your escape, if you could just tell us briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I can. When it got dark and when those excavators came and when started killing under the lights, then I stayed a bit further away, ten or 15 metres away from those lights so there was no light cast on me. I got out from under the dead bodies, and then I crawled for about ten metres where the dead bodies were. There were these bushes about one metre tall. Behind this bush there was a bit of shrubbery, perhaps a little tree. Then I hid there so even if they would turn on the lights, they couldn't see me. I turned around and then I watched them doing what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you -- did you know about approximately where you were at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know where I was. I mean, I didn't even know what place this was or how far away it was from Zvornik. I knew that I was -- it was on the left-hand side. Then Tuzla would be on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall anything distinctive about anything that you observed while you were making your escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: While I was lying there, I was watching this, and I saw this high iron fence and there was a road underneath, but I could not see what was there. There was this poplar tree above me, so I couldn't realise what it was that was there. Later on whether I told people in Tuzla, they told me that this is actually an underpass underneath a railway so that that was the fence of the railroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I just have 65 ter 1707 shown to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Right. This kind of fence, yes. Now, is it a railroad or is it a road? Whatever. I saw this fence or railing as I was lying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does the area, that is what's depicted in the photograph, is that similar to the area or the area that you were there that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: It is similar, it is similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to your escape, did you escape alone or did you escape with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: There was this other man too who was alive. When the last little TAM truck came, it stood there, it didn't go back. When all these people were killed, there was no more gunfire, then what was said was there is no one left at the gym, everybody was brought here, then one of these soldiers said should we come with you or should we stay behind? And this voice said, no one said that you should come with me and you're not going. If another vehicle comes to pick you up, then you won't be here anyway and if another vehicle doesn't come, you will stand guard here until the morning. So this little TAM truck left. I continued to lie there. They got close to those excavators and then they were smoking. A bit later, there were lights on again and again you could hear the truck coming. A similar little TAM truck came and they boarded the truck and left. Oh, yes they turned off the lights of the excavator, the sky became clear, there was moonlight, and then I got up and I started shouting, is anyone alive? If someone is alive, let's go. And then all of a sudden I heard a voice from the heap of dead bodies, and he said there's me, and we got up and left. Behind us, there was a bit of a thicket, and he said, let's go by this grave uphill and I said, I can't walk, I have a bad leg. Let's go through a better place where the woods are not so thick. So then we went along this pasture land and there was a lot of grass there, and as we were walking through the grass we looked around and this man said to me, they will see that we escaped. And I said well what can I do about it? I can't go uphill now when there is this forest, and then when we -- we saw where there were lots of trees and where there were few trees. We took a bit of a break --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, and I know you have a lot to say but do you -- did you learn this person's name at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you meet anybody else during your escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning, yet another man joined us, from the same execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if I could just pop into private session for a second? And then out again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to these two individuals, did you arrive in the free territory together with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was that, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: On the 19th, I think it was a Wednesday, but again I'm not sure. I knew that but it's been a long time, and it's hard for me to remember all of this with certainty. I think it was a Wednesday, on the 19th, but now I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I don't have any further questions for you, so I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Now I have on my list all the Defence teams. Let me go through the list. Mr. Zivanovic, you asked for 30 minutes. Will you stick to that or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that I will finish by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then go ahead. One moment because you have a missile.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. My name is Zoran Zivanovic, and I'm Defence counsel for Vujadin Popovic in this trial. I'm going to put a few questions to you in relation to your testimony. You testified that in 1982, you had an accident and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I remain disabled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, because of that, you were singled out in Potocari into this group of men who -- that consisted of the elderly and disabled, am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, you were a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether while you were a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you had weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I found that you made your first statement about all of this on the 21st of July 1995, to the Ministry of the Interior, or, rather, the department of the Ministry of the Interior in Zivinice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have a look at this statement of yours, 1D440. You're going to see it now on the screen. I beg your pardon. It's the 25th of July. It wasn't the 21st, the 25th. That's when the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And it was given to the state security sector in Tuzla. That is what is stated here. Could you please look at the bottom of this statement? There is a signature there. Could you please tell me whether it's your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is. Could you please now look at the last page, page 4, of this statement in e-court? We are just going to look at the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It says here this statement has been read back to me and I have participated in its formulation myself. I therefore accept it as my own which I confirm with my signature, and am willing to repeat it before a court: Underneath it there is your signature again, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we just go back to the first page now, the first page of this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 1 of your statement? This introduction and then it says statement, and could we look at the second sentence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It reads as follows: "I was a member of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina until the demilitarisation of Srebrenica and until it was declared a protected -- a safe haven, when I turned in my weapons."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I mean until those people who had weapons handed them in, whereas I did not have any weapons at all. I was disabled. I was in the medical service along with the wounded. So that I could say fetch some water for them or light a fire for them when it was cold, and when they surrendered their weapons, well, this is a bit of a mistake. However, regardless of the mistake, I did say that, when we surrendered our weapons. But I was referring to all the soldiers who had surrendered their weapons. I myself due to my disability, could not have had any weapons. I was just there to help in the mess and in the medical service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that you are not denying that you've stated what is written here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes. But they surrendered the weapons. It wasn't that we surrendered the weapons. When they surrendered their weapons and when there was demilitarisation. Until then I was no longer a member of the army. That's just a small mistake that was made. When they did, not when we did. I don't know who actually wrote this. I really cannot walk without a cane for a hundred metres, so I was there helping out in the mess so that I could help say wounded people, fetch some water for them, light a fire, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Along with this sentence, where it says, "When I handed over my weapon," it says, "From then on, I was not armed."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Well, all of this that is written, I believe that was written, but from then on, no one was armed. But now what they wrote about me, well, that's different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you claiming that from the moment when the demilitarisation of Srebrenica was proclaimed, no one was armed any longer? Because everybody surrendered their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: As far as I know, everybody surrendered their weapons and now as for what I don't know, well...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about something else now. From Potocari, from this house where you were, when you were singled out with these other elderly and disabled men you were taken to this warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, how big was this room, this warehouse where you were put up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: If it's stated anywhere in my statement how large the room was, I say that that was how large it was. Now, I've forgotten. I really couldn't say. It's been eight or nine years since then. So I cannot give you the size of the room. It was a large room. I am not able to tell you now, but if I ever mentioned the size of the room in my statement previously, that's how big it was. Now, if I were to estimate it, I would say it was more than 15 metres, up to 20 metres, and it was eight metres wide but it's -- I'm not sure. It was a long time ago. It's something that I've forgotten now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we were to compare it to the room where you were put in Potocari, was that warehouse bigger or smaller?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: It was bigger. We couldn't all fit into the house. There were more people, three times as many people in front of the house than in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you compared the warehouse with the school or the gym where you were, can you say if it was bigger or the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: It was smaller, much smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, this warehouse, the way you described it according to how you remember it, it was at one point completely full and you were there at the time as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And there were about 400 people inside at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: According to my estimate, because later there were 296 when we were leaving the warehouse so that's almost 300. At, I think that in a 24 hour period, about 80 were killed and then those ten who were taken out in the morning and the ten who were taken out in the evening, so it's 100 that went missing, they were not with us. So it was almost 400 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were in the gym, which was in Orahovac, can you please tell me if the soldiers who were guarding you were inside the gym or outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: They were outside. They were at the entrance, at both entrances. There were two each. And then some would just come up to the door and they would observe and then they would leave, but there were two posted at each door and they did not enter the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, if you remember, when you were taken out, when you were -- when was it your turn to leave that gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Well, again, it's something that I've forgotten. Perhaps in my first statement, I told you what -- how it was correctly. I gave you the time, but now I'm unable to tell you. It's possible, from what I can remember, that the sun was still high and that it was probably between 5.00 or 6.00, but I cannot remember that now. But I do confirm that in my first statement, if I said the time, then I confirm that that would be the correct time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to remember -- I'm going to remind you of that statement. Just give me a moment, please. I want to find it. It's the same document, 1D440, page 3. The second paragraph, you can see a sentence that says, it's in the second paragraph, line 6, "I came, it was my turn at around 2000 hours." And you said the same thing, I think you said the same thing four days before then, when you were giving your first statement to the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I stand by my first statement. I cannot stand by what I'm saying right now. I mean, it was ten years ago. I confirm my first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more thing I'm going to ask you. You said that you saw on a number of occasions, during all of these difficult events that you went through, that you saw General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And now, I saw that in one place in the transcript, you said that you saw him six times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: In total, during those three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Three -- six times during those three days. And I'm interested in the last time that you saw him, and that was on that day when you were executed, and when you saw him the last time, according to what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me now that if that was still in the day-time or was it already dark or were the lights on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: It was still day-time. It was nice. The excavators hadn't arrived yet. It was still day-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately, once the execution was carried out, after you fell, was that after that? How long after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. The shortest on the list would be the Pandurevic team. Do you still intend to cross-examine this witness, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic or Mr. Meek? I don't know who will be dealing with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We could go ahead and start today if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Dobar dan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, you've just testified a few moments ago at page 75, on today's transcript, lines 5 through 7, that -- and you said, "All right. Very well. I stand by my first statement. I cannot stand by what I'm saying right now. I mean, it was ten years ago. I confirm my first statement." Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot always tell you the exact time. About the time that I said, I confirm the time that I gave in my first statement. As for the time right now, I cannot always remember exactly what time it was, but it's in my first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Are you sure you're not in that statement claiming that you stand by your first statement and that you confirm that first statement, and you cannot stand by anything you said today, including the time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Only the time, not the other things. The rest, what I'm saying today, and in my present testimony, in my first statement, I stand by everything that I said there, but if you ask me what time did you go there, what time did you leave, what time did you get there? This is something that I cannot remember exactly. As for what I'm talking about, about what happened, I stand by what I am saying now. I have always stood by every statement that I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask this question: If all these years later --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: -- you cannot be sure about the times or various times, how can you be so sure about the various numbers that you've given us today in court, of the other people that were with you in this location or that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: What was more or less important what time I left, what time I came, I wasn't interested in that so much. So perhaps I forgot that. But the crime that took place is something I can never forgets and the people who were there, who were these people, I cannot forget that until the day I die. The horrors that were there were where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately the time that you left Bratunac on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I left Bratunac when the lights were coming on, in the town. That's when I left. As for the time, I didn't look at a watch. That's when we entered the buses, and we waited, and then when the lights began to come on, that's when we set off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, at that point in time, were you familiar at all with what time the lights normally came on in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And again, you will agree with me, sir, that this -- these events that you've described today, being in the gym, in the first warehouse, taken to the gym, that it was a very confusing time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I don't know what would be confusing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, according to your testimony, there were a lot of people in a small area, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you didn't know what was going to happen to you, and everybody else didn't know what was going to happen to them, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: We didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Were you concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: How could we not be concerned? First they started killing in Bratunac, so we weren't even thinking that anyone would survive that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Besides being concerned, you were worried, correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And again, if you can answer me yes or no, not only were you worried about yourself, you were worried about your family, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You hadn't had much sleep or rest in the period 24, 48 hours before this, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Correct, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And according to your testimony, you were under a disability, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And were you on medication before you took off to head towards the free territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: I never used medication. I have a leg injury that cannot be treated. So I have a disability, but I do not require any medicines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Very lucky for you, sir. Does the leg injury which led to your disability, does it cause you pain in your leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Always, if I'm sitting, and my leg is down, then it swells up. Only when I'm lying down, then the circulation improves. When I hold my head -- my leg horizontally. If I am sitting for a long time and my legs are bent or they are down, then I experience discomfort.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And sir, you would agree with me that you were experiencing discomfort in your leg during the time period that we're talking about, being, as you've told us, jammed in small areas and buses and the school, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And even through your -- all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have to stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can I have one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But there is a trial in the afternoon, go ahead with your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Again, sir, just to sum this up, you had a lot on your mind, you were worried about yourself and your family, you were scared, you were concerned, your leg was hurting you, you hadn't had much sleep for a few days and I put it to you, sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-169
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: -- you have to agree with me, I think that you really don't know how many people were in that school, it's just something you heard, those numbers you heard, once you reached the free territory, fair statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the gym or in the warehouse? In the gym, we estimated. I always said nobody counted but we made an estimate because it was an enormous room and as the others were saying, they said there is over 2.500 people here. That's what I said. Nobody counted. As for Bratunac, we were counted so I'm giving you exact figures, and you will see that in the statement, if there is one missing, then you can say that I'm not speaking the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you very much. I just wanted to make sure that other people told you they estimated that. Thank you very much for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will continue tomorrow, Mr. Meek. Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Together, it's not my estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 2nd day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
